exposure: determinants of obstructed labour outcomes (unbooked status, parity, maternal age, education, rural residence)
cohort: The study included 214 women diagnosed with obstructed labour managed at Ebonyi State University Teaching Hospital Abakaliki between January 2007 and December 2011.
finding: The primary finding was that cephalopelvic disproportion was the commonest cause of obstructed labour, occurring more in primiparous women, with wound infection as the most frequent maternal complication, while most neonates had good Apgar scores.
